𝗔𝗞𝗕𝗔𝗬𝗔𝗡 𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗦𝗧 𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗡𝗘𝗦𝗘 𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗦𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗢𝗙 𝗪𝗣𝗦 𝗙𝗜𝗦𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗦: 𝗕𝗔𝗖𝗞 𝗧𝗢 𝗜𝗧𝗦 𝗢𝗟𝗗 𝗩𝗜𝗢𝗟𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗛𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗦

“After China’s water-and-biscuit-giving drama and propaganda in the West Philippine Sea last December, which no one bought, it is back to its old violent habits of harassing Filipino fishers.”

This was the statement issued today by Akbayan Party President Rafaela David, condemning the latest incident of Chinese harassment in the West Philippine Sea. A China Coast Guard vessel, accompanied by a PLA Navy ship, harassed a Filipino fishing boat operating well within Philippine waters on January 12, 2026. This marks the first recorded harassment incident of 2026 and yet another reminder that China’s aggression remains the gravest threat to the safety of Filipino fisherfolk.

“No amount of drama and propaganda can conceal the true nature of a foreign aggressor in our own seas. China’s latest harassment of fishers who are simply trying to make an honest living is proof of this. China is the single greatest threat to the lives and livelihoods of our fisherfolk in the area. Let there be no more doubt about it,” David said.

David, who is also the co-convenor of Atin Ito, a civil society coalition that organized three historic civilian-led supply missions to the West Philippine Sea, lauded the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) for its swift response to the incident.

“We recognize the PCG’s immediate assistance and rescue of our fisherfolk. Once again, our frontliners showed that in the face of foreign aggression, Filipino bayanihan remains one of our strongest and most principled responses,” she added.

David also called on the Philippine government to immediately file a diplomatic protest against China. “We urge the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) to lodge a strong diplomatic protest over this latest incident. Instead of concocting drama and propaganda, the Chinese Embassy in Manila would do better to explain why China continues to harass Filipino fishers and intrude into waters that are indisputably ours,” David asserted.

#AkbayanPartylist
